---
title: "Version Control"
order: 2
---

### V1 — All project code under git

The throwaway script made a figure. The one-off that produced Figure 3 is the one you need again for the revision. Track everything from the first commit. It costs nothing and saves the panic later.

```bash
git init
git add analysis.py figures.R
git commit -m "Initial analysis pipeline"
```

### V3 — Main branch always runs

A colleague may pull at any moment. Keep main runnable at all times. Do risky work on a branch and merge only once it passes. Whoever pulls next inherits working code, not your half-finished state.

```bash
git switch -c fix-outlier-filter
# ...work, run tests...
git switch main
git merge fix-outlier-filter   # only once green
```

### V4 — Shared remote org, not personal accounts

Access outlives any one person. Host repos under a lab organization instead of a personal account. Permissions and continuity then survive graduations, and nobody chases a former student for admin rights.

```bash
# lab org remote, not a personal account
git remote add origin \
  git@github.com:adamolab/saccade-model.git
```
